answer.rationale: Memory c2 is the relevant prior on this vendor: switching to the low-cost primary cut unit cost sharply last year, onboarding was quick, and invoicing stayed accurate. That directly informs whether the 14-day window is sufficient for a switch given no auto-renew. Memory c4 (renegotiate) and memory c5 (defer) are weaker fits here: renegotiating the incumbent cannot meet the 18% mandate on its own (the low-cost vendor's quote meets it alone), and deferring does not solve the contract expiry. I do not want to commit c2 from memory alone — I want the archived source verified — but if it holds, c2 is a strong prior that this kind of switch has worked cleanly before at this organization. I am naming switch_primary_vendor as the intended action pending verification, with a small guarded test framing to keep delivery risk bounded against the 94% utilization / zero buffer posture.
